input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Notebook activity data source for idle-workbench reporting

## Description

Makes the notebook controller's existing per-workbench last-activity tracking
consumable by platform consumers, so the RHOAI web console can build a
per-project idle-workbench report from it. The controller already tracks last
activity per kernel through Jupyter server API probes (this is what the idle
culler uses); this epic validates that the data is readable through a
supported interface and, where it is not, exposes it — for example on the
Notebook custom resource — without changing culling behavior.

## Scope

- Determine how the notebook controller records last-activity data today and
  whether consumers of the Notebook custom resource can already read it.
- Surface the per-workbench last-activity timestamp through a supported,
  documented consumer interface if it is not already readable, keeping the
  idle culler's behavior and configuration unchanged.
- Verify the activity data is correct for workbenches in mixed states:
  recently used, idle, stopped, and never used.
- Document the interface semantics for consuming teams (update cadence, and
  what a missing value means).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with workbenches in mixed states (recently used, idle,
  stopped, never used), a platform consumer can retrieve each workbench's
  last-activity timestamp through a documented interface, and the retrieved
  values reconcile with the controller's activity tracking (recently used
  workbenches show recent timestamps; idle ones show old timestamps).
- Workbenches with no recorded activity are distinguishable from workbenches
  with recorded activity in the exposed data.
- The exposure does not alter existing idle-culler behavior: culling
  continues to function with the same defaults and per-workbench overrides
  as before.
- The interface and its semantics are documented for consuming teams.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): enabling epic — provides the data source (notebook controller
  activity tracking) that the per-project idle-workbench report in the web
  console is built from. Inherits P1 by priority inheritance.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console

## Description

Adds a per-project idle-workbench report to the RHOAI web console. For each
workbench in a project, the report shows last activity, owner, and reserved
resources, sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking, so
administrators can see which workbenches are sitting idle and reclaim
capacity with confidence. Includes CSV export of the report for
administrators.

## Scope

- New report view in the console, scoped per project, listing each workbench
  with its last activity (from the notebook controller's activity data),
  owner, and reserved resources, presented so administrators can identify
  idle workbenches.
- Owner and reserved resources are read from the Notebook custom resources;
  last activity comes from the consumable notebook-controller activity data
  source.
- CSV export of the report: administrators can download the report contents
  as a CSV file.
- The report is read-only — no reclamation or deletion action is offered
  (automated reclamation is out of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, the console shows an
  idle-workbench report listing each workbench's last activity, owner, and
  reserved resources.
- Report contents reconcile with the underlying data: owner and reserved
  resources match the Notebook custom resources, and last activity matches
  the notebook controller's activity data source.
- Given the report, an administrator can export it as CSV; the exported file
  contains the same rows and columns as the displayed report and opens in
  standard spreadsheet tooling.
- The report offers no automated reclamation or deletion action, consistent
  with the strategy's out-of-scope list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): fully covered — per-project idle-workbench report (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of this report is bundled into this epic
  rather than split out — the export renders the same report data on the same
  report view this epic builds, so splitting it would double-touch the same
  UI surface and data structure.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the web console

## Description

Adds a stale pipeline-run report to the RHOAI web console. The report lists
completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age, together with their
retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata, so
administrators can see where storage is accumulating. Includes CSV export of
the report for administrators.

## Scope

- New report view in the console, scoped per project, listing completed
  pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold, with each run's
  age/completion information and its retained artifacts.
- Data is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata via the KFP v2 REST
  API, the documented interface the console already uses to surface pipeline
  runs.
- The staleness age threshold is configurable; where the threshold is
  configured (per-project administrator setting vs. deployment-level
  default) is an implementation decision for the Dashboard team.
- CSV export of the report: administrators can download the report contents
  as a CSV file.
- The report is read-only — no deletion or reclamation action is offered
  (automated reclamation is out of scope for the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of varying ages, the console
  shows a stale pipeline-run report listing the completed runs older than the
  configured age, including their retained artifacts.
- The staleness age threshold is configurable, and changing it changes which
  runs appear in the report.
- Report contents reconcile with Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata (completion
  state and timestamps, artifact references) — this validates the pipelines
  component as a correct, working data source.
- Given the report, an administrator can export it as CSV; the exported file
  contains the same rows and columns as the displayed report and opens in
  standard spreadsheet tooling.
- The report offers no automated reclamation or deletion action, consistent
  with the strategy's out-of-scope list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): fully covered — stale pipeline-run report (completed runs
  older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2, bundled): CSV export of this report is bundled into this epic
  rather than split out — the export renders the same report data on the same
  report view this epic builds, so splitting it would double-touch the same
  UI surface and data structure.

# Documentation for the idle and stale resource reports

## Description

Documents the new console reports — the per-project idle-workbench report
and the stale pipeline-run report — so cluster administrators understand what
the reports show and can reclaim capacity safely. Covers how to read each
report, how to configure the staleness age, how to use CSV export, and the
safe manual reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs.

## Scope

Content outline:

- New documentation topic for the idle-workbench report: what it shows (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources per workbench), where to find it in
  the console, and how administrators interpret it to find idle workbenches.
- New documentation topic for the stale pipeline-run report: what it shows
  (completed runs older than the configured age, with retained artifacts),
  where to find it, and how to configure the staleness age threshold.
- CSV export usage for both reports.
- Safe reclamation steps: documented manual cleanup guidance for idle
  workbenches and stale pipeline runs/artifacts, consistent with the
  strategy's out-of-scope boundary (no automated reclamation or deletion, no
  cost/chargeback calculations).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains both reports and their data columns, and the
  described behavior matches the implemented console reports.
- Documentation explains how to configure the stale-run age threshold and
  how to export either report as CSV.
- Documentation includes safe manual reclamation steps for idle workbenches
  and stale pipeline runs, clearly framed as manual actions with appropriate
  cautions.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented reports by the
  engineering team before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): fully covered — documentation explains the reports and safe
  reclamation steps.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016: Idle resource reporting in the web console

Triage (Step 0): neither check fired. The strategy is not below threshold —
it spans three components (web console, notebook controller, Kubeflow
Pipelines) owned by three distinct teams, and the scope contains multiple
architecturally distinct work streams (console UI reporting over two
disparate data sources, plus substantive documentation). It is not
documentation-only — code changes are required in the console. Full
decomposition (Steps 1-8) was executed.

## Step 1 Parse Notes

The strategy is compact: HLR table, affected-component list, out-of-scope
list, and an explicit "Open Questions: None". Health warnings for missing
sections are recorded below (Health Warnings).

| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (artifact consumer) | E001 produces the consumable last-activity data source (a surface on the Notebook CR) that the idle-workbench report's code reads; the console report builds against it, so the epics are serial. |

| (no edge) E001 ∥ E003 | Rule 14 | Different repos and components with no shared artifacts — the stale-run report reads KFP run metadata, not notebook activity data. Parallel. |

## Component Mapping and Passive-Component Handling

Canonical component names (from `.context/rhai-components.txt`) mapped from

| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | RHOAI Dashboard |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Workbenches |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | RHOAI Pipelines |

Active/passive classification:

- **Dashboard — active.** All new report UI and CSV export code lives here;
  generates E002 and E003.
- **Notebooks (notebook controller) — passive, validated by a different
  team.** The controller already tracks last activity (architecture context:
  `notebooks.md` — "last activity tracked per kernel through Jupyter server
  API probes", consumed internally by the idle culler). No culling-behavior
  change is requested. Per the Step 2 exception, because the consuming epic
  is owned by the RHOAI Dashboard team while the data source is owned by the

- **Data Science Pipelines — passive, validated as an acceptance criterion.**
  Run completion metadata is reachable through the documented KFP v2 REST
  API, an interface the console already consumes to surface pipeline runs
  (`data-science-pipelines.md`). No separate cross-team validation epic is
